name: nuSTORM
summary: nuSTORM is a proposed stored-muon neutrino facility for precision electron- and muon-flavour scattering, with an implementation at CERN studied through Physics Beyond Colliders.
physics_targets: Precision neutrino-nucleus cross sections for oscillation experiments
Light sterile-neutrino searches and muon-accelerator development
detection_principle: Pions injected into a storage ring decay into muons that are captured and circulate. Muon decays in a straight section provide neutrinos of known flavour composition; stored-muon instrumentation constrains the flux and changing the muon momentum scans the spectrum.

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The 2025 strategy submission describes a design and proposed implementation at CERN.

timeline.event: CERN implementation and updated physics case submitted

phases.name: Original Fermilab nuSTORM proposal
phases.description: The 2013 Fermilab proposal was an earlier site and detector design; its parameters should not be mixed with the later CERN Physics Beyond Colliders version.

results.summary: Reported a facility design and projected physics programme; no operating nuSTORM neutrino storage ring is established by these sources.

science_scope: The record describes the named experiment as one programme; detector subsystems and repeated analyses are not counted as independent experiments.
